nodes.label: dsh-mobile (mobile host for the DSH ecosystem)
Static plugin manifest
nodes.rationale: Reading the manifest must never execute code; capability negotiation against the RuntimeDescriptor happens before activation so an under-privileged plugin fails visibly, never silently.

nodes.label: Install transaction and append-only receipt journal
nodes.rationale: Install is a content-addressed, crash-safe transaction mirroring upstream desktopPnpm.installPlugin recovery-receipt semantics: the receipt write is the commit point and pending receipts are replayed at startup, so a host never leaves a crash half-examined.

nodes.label: Capability Gateway (gateway@1)
nodes.rationale: The gateway is host-fixed and never a plugin, with a deliberately narrow table: platform branching (hostType conditionals, RFC 0002 anti-pattern) is banned by construction because there is nothing to branch on; every primitive is typed, permission-flagged, and mandatorily audited.

nodes.label: httpFetch streaming primitive
nodes.rationale: The response body is an async iterable of byte chunks so streaming is one event sequence, never a blocking whole-result (D8); abort() rejects the pending promise with cancelled.

nodes.label: wasmRun in-process WebAssembly primitive
nodes.rationale: iOS forbids JIT and the architecture refuses subprocesses (D2), so the alternative to an in-process interpreter is no WebAssembly at all; the pure-function ABI (input string, dsh.emit output, i32 status) keeps it a seam rather than a sandbox escape.

nodes.label: ishRun emulated Linux userland primitive
nodes.rationale: A userspace interpreter emulates both guest instructions and syscalls inside the app process (no child process, no second OS, no JIT - D2), which is the only way iOS can run a real Alpine userland; the audit boundary moves and the contract requires the host to state what per-call audit cannot reach inside the guest.

nodes.label: GatewayError codes (fail-loud rule)
nodes.rationale: Unknown codes are fatal and must surface loudly - receivers never fall back on an error code they do not recognize; user dismissal is a value (null / approved:false), not an error.

nodes.label: RuntimeDescriptor (honest capability surface)
nodes.rationale: Absence is information for negotiation, never faked: a host declares what it cannot do and plugins see the gap, which is what lets iOS, Android and HarmonyOS share one contract without platform branches.

nodes.label: Harness core on QuickJS (single-threaded coroutine runtime)
nodes.rationale: quickjs-ng (pure-C interpreter, no JIT) over nodejs-mobile: an order of magnitude less memory, no JIT gray zones, multi-runtime isolation (D1); the dedicated serial thread keeps every callback auditable and nothing blocks the runtime.

nodes.label: Loopback carrier (HTTP/WS + WebView presentation)
nodes.rationale: WKWebView runs in an Apple-privileged process where JIT is legal, and the official React frontend is reused with zero changes because it only knows the loopback HTTP/WS protocol, never the host.

nodes.label: Event-driven execution rules (D8)
nodes.rationale: Direct module calls and blocking whole-result APIs couple components and kill substitutability; polling wastes battery and races. LLM token deltas, tool runs and subagents must report progress as event sequences, and checkpoint is defined as event queue drained.

nodes.label: Log-based E2E verification (no screenshots)
nodes.rationale: CI asserts on structured logs with a unique scenario-id and a one-to-one expected-logged match: screenshots are unverifiable in CI, the log stream is the same surface the logging gate governs, and the list of unmatched entries is itself the diagnosis.

nodes.label: Per-plugin QuickJS runtime isolation
nodes.rationale: One QuickJS runtime per plugin with zero sharing and all system access through the gateway makes dsh-mobile the first host in the ecosystem with technically enforced permissions rather than convention.

nodes.label: Three UI plugin levels (config / component / whole)
Multi-platform capability-negotiation strategy
nodes.rationale: contract/, runtime/, system-plugins/ and presentation/ are platform-independent JS reused one-copy-three-platforms; each platform adds only its privileged layer, primitive bindings and native shell, and all differences are expressed via capability negotiation - hostType branching is banned (RFC 0002 anti-pattern).

nodes.label: D1 quickjs-ng as mobile JS engine
D3 UI is a Web Client plugin in WKWebView
D4 distribution outside the App Store
D6 pinned upstream + outboard implementation packages
D8 all modules event-driven including streaming
D9 upstream DSH packages ported verbatim, never reimplemented
D10 release-please drives the version stream (superseded)
D11 release-please with GITHUB_TOKEN (corrected by D13)
D12 release triggered by v* tag push
D13 required check must come from the PR own events
D14 version bump as ordinary PR, release-please retired
D16 emulated Linux userland adopted with licence and audit consequences named
Runtime spine (mountSpine over verbatim vendored packages)
E2E acceptance bar (one-to-one log compare + deliverables)
Tag-push release pipeline (release/ios, release/android, release/harmony)
nodes.rationale: The tag push is the release trigger because a release depending on something else completing (a credential, a repository setting, a suppressed event) stops silently exactly where this pipeline spent days; cutting a release needs nothing but contents:write and a failed attempt is retried by pushing again.

nodes.label: dev/* and release/* GitHub Actions workflows
Route table (exact / longest-prefix / fallback / upgrade)
nodes.rationale: Named routes compose to be disjoint, so a duplicate (kind, path) throws - a collision is a misconfiguration, not a precedence question; matching is fixed (exact, then longest prefix, then fallback) so registration order changes nothing.

nodes.label: HarmonyOS NEXT host (M5, ArkTS + NAPI + ArkWeb)
iOS host (SwiftUI shell + privileged layer + gateway + carrier)
official-web (vendored official UI dist + 58-package client bundles)
Swappable-UI acceptance criterion
nodes.rationale: Zero hardcoded UI in the host: which Web Client is active is configuration and the official frontend is merely the default plugin (D3), proven by the config-selected client swap and component-level slot registration.

nodes.label: gateway.js (typed JS shim over the bridge)
upstream/ system layer for the verbatim port (D9)
nodes.rationale: Upstream packages run verbatim, so all adaptation (shims, boot, scripted seams standing in for Node.js platform services) lives on our side of the port, mirroring dsh-desktop role as thin host; zero vendored edits keeps re-pins cheap.
